references.text: Here is described the actual making of the same utensils that were commanded in 27:3—the ash basins, shovels, bowls, forks, and fire pans, all made of bronze.
Refers to the utensils used at the altar, including fire pans, forks, shovels, and bowls, which the Levites were to take care of.
Hiram made similar utensils of bronze for Solomon's temple, including pots, shovels, and bowls.
Parallel account of Hiram's work in making temple utensils of bronze, including pots, shovels, and bowls.
Mentions the same types of utensils—fire pans, ash basins, shovels, and bowls—that were taken from the temple to Babylon.
Describes the temple utensils that were carried away to Babylon, including the pots, shovels, knives, bowls, and fire pans.
27:19 generalizes the principle of bronze from the specific utensils in 27:3 to all the equipment of the sanctuary.
Jeremiah documents the plundering of the same types of bronze vessels that were commanded in Exodus, marking the end of their service.
